context: Telephone enquiry about an evening course at an adult learning centre

cues.t: Part 1. You will hear a man telephoning an adult learning centre to ask about an evening course. First you have some time to look at questions 1 to 10.
You will see that there is an example that has been done for you. On this occasion only, the conversation relating to this will be played first.
Good evening, Bramley Adult Learning Centre. Sophie speaking.
Hi there. I'd like to sign up for one of your evening courses, if there's still space.
Let's see what we can do. Can I have your name, please?
Yes, it's Ian Prentice. P-R-E-N-T-I-C-E.

The man's surname is Prentice, so Prentice has been written in the space. Now we shall begin. You should answer the questions as you listen, because you will not hear the recording a second time. Listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 10.
Good evening, Bramley Adult Learning Centre. Sophie speaking.
Hi there. I'd like to sign up for one of your evening courses, if there's still space.
Let's see what we can do. Can I have your name, please?
Yes, it's Ian Prentice. P-R-E-N-T-I-C-E.
Thanks, Mr Prentice. Which course were you interested in?
I was hoping to do watercolour painting, but your website says it's full.
It is, I'm afraid. There's a waiting list of about twenty people.
Oh well. In that case, I'll try something I've always fancied. Are there any places left on the beginners' pottery course?
Yes, plenty. Now, the brochure gives the first class as the 1st of September, but the tutor can't make that date, so the course will start a week later, on the 8th.
The 8th of September. That's fine. And the classes are on Thursdays, aren't they?
They used to be, but another group needs the kiln that day. So it's every Monday now, from half past seven until half past nine.
Monday suits me. Where do I go? The brochure says Room C7.
That's been changed as well, I'm sorry. C7 was far too small, so this year you'll be in Room B12, on the ground floor of the new block.
Is the new block the one beside the main entrance?
That's right, the brick building on your left as you come in. There'll be signs up during the first week, and someone on the front desk to point you in the right direction.
B12. Got it. And what's the fee for the course?
The full price for the ten weeks is 195 pounds. Are you working at the moment?
No, I retired in June.
Then you qualify for our reduced rate, which is 165 pounds.
165. That's very welcome. Does that include everything?
It covers your tuition, the use of all the tools, and firing your work in the kiln. The one thing you'll pay for separately is clay. You buy it from the tutor, by the bag, whenever you need it.
Roughly how much does a bag cost?
Only a few pounds, and one bag lasts most people several weeks, so it won't add much to your costs.
Fair enough. Should I bring anything with me? An apron, perhaps?
Most people find an apron doesn't cover enough, and we provide the towels. What the tutor recommends is an old shirt with long sleeves, to keep your clothes clean.
I've got plenty of those. Who's the tutor, by the way? A friend of mine did a class with a Mr Barker.
Mr Barker retired last summer. It's Mrs Fenwick now. That's F-E-N-W-I-C-K. She's very good.
And how many students are there in a group?
We keep it to twelve, because there are only twelve wheels. Everyone gets their own place, and she'll show you how to use it in the very first lesson.
That sounds ideal. I've never touched a potter's wheel in my life.
Most of the group will be complete beginners too, so you won't feel out of place.
Great. And is there anywhere to park? I noticed some parking meters outside.
The signs in the car park say you have to pay until eight o'clock, but they're out of date. The council changed the rules in the spring, and parking is now free after 7 p.m.
That's good news, because the class doesn't start until half past seven anyway.
Exactly. Most of our evening students arrive at around twenty past.
Excellent. So how do I enrol? Can I do it now, over the phone?
We stopped taking bookings by phone last year, I'm afraid. You'll need to fill in the enrolment form on our website. It only takes five minutes.
No problem, I'll do that tonight. Thanks very much for your help.
That is the end of Part 1. You now have half a minute to check your answers.
